findings.problem: Driven and printed, not read: emulateMedia('print') plus page.pdf({format:'A4'}) returns TWO pages. The sheet lays out at 1439.8px tall inside a 794px stage; an A4 page at 96dpi is 1123px. The rail is guillotined between '51 Final guest numbers' and '65 Venue walk-through' — page 2 opens with an orphaned rail stub carrying no couple name, no date, no heading and no page mark, and its lower 40% is blank paper. I enumerated every rule in every sheet from the live document: zero CSSPageRule, zero @media print blocks, zero break-inside or page-break declarations anywhere in shell.css or b.css. The only artifact this product makes that cannot be reflowed after it exists is the one medium with no CSS behind it. The 794px stage is A4's width honoured; A4's height was never honoured. Seven fixture moments already spill; a real wedding-morning running order of thirty moments is four unmanaged pages.
findings.fix: Add a print layer to b.css: '@page { size: A4; margin: 14mm 16mm; }' plus '@media print { html,body{background:#fff} .tl-caption{display:none} .b-print{padding:0;max-width:none} .b-item,.b-behindRow{break-inside:avoid} .b-measureHead,.b-behindHead{break-after:avoid} .b-two{break-inside:avoid} }'. Give the sheet running furniture that only paper sees: a repeating head 'Mara & Finn · Saturday 3 October 2026' from page 2 on, and a mono page mark ('2 of 2'). Then re-render the PDF and assert both the page count and that no .b-item box straddles a page boundary — this is measurable, so it belongs in interaction-check.mjs as an assertion that opens the real PDF, not a 794px screenshot.

findings.problem: The gate asserts 'the keepsake prints a link that can be typed'. On real paper it prints https://timeline.signalstudio.ie/s/j7Qm2vK4xR9bT1nL6yH3cW8pZ5sD0aG7fJ4uE2rN9tM — forty-three case-sensitive random characters — and at the sheet's measure it wraps mid-token after 'sD0aG7fJ4' onto a second mono line with no hyphen, no continuation mark and no visual join. A guest holding this sheet in a church cannot reach the live plan: they must transcribe forty-three characters with correct case, and the wrap gives them no way to know whether the break is a break or a character. The assertion is true of the string and false of the object. This is the only bridge from the paper artifact back to the product, and it is broken.
findings.fix: On the printed sheet only, replace the raw token with two things on one line: a human short code in the mono face at the title step, spaced every four characters ('timeline.signalstudio.ie/s/  MARA 7K4Q', resolving server-side to the same share id, case-insensitive), and beside it a QR block rendered as pure ink — a 24mm square of #111111 modules on paper, which introduces no hue and no weight and so clears the palette lock. Keep the full URL nowhere on the sheet. Set '.b-printLink { overflow-wrap: normal; word-break: keep-all }' so nothing can wrap mid-code, and assert in the gate that the printed link string is at most 44 characters and contains no line break.

findings.problem: Judged as a physical object, the sheet's whole vocabulary is one the paper cannot honour. Its hero is 79 at 148px with DAYS beside it; the rule beneath reads 'TODAY IS 16 JULY'; the measure is headed 'DAYS AWAY'; and every mono numeral down the left column (16, 23, 37, 44, 51, 65, 79) is a distance from that today. A screen re-renders those numbers every morning. Paper does not. The morning after it leaves the printer every number on the sheet is wrong, and the sheet does not know it — the only other date on it is the footer's 'UPDATED 15 JULY 2026', which is the plan's last edit, not the print. So the object carries two dates, neither of which says 'this is when this sheet was true', and the largest thing on it is the fact that decays fastest. The screen's language was ported to paper without asking what paper can hold.
findings.fix: Branch the vocabulary on medium, not only the scale. In render-b.js states.print, when medium is 'print': make the hero the date itself ('Saturday 3 October 2026' at the display step) with '79 days away' demoted to the sub-line; change the rule from 'TODAY IS 16 JULY' to 'PRINTED 16 JULY 2026'; change the measure heading from 'DAYS AWAY' to 'THE DAYS'; and swap the left mono column from the day-count to the calendar date ('1 AUG', '8 AUG', '22 AUG'), which the row already carries as its sub-line — so drop the duplicated 'SAT 1 AUG' line and put the weekday in the column. Every proportional gap and every tick stays exactly as it is; only the numerals change from a relative fact to an absolute one. Then the sheet is still true in October.

findings.element: shell.css :root tokens vs b.css (197 selectors, 1 custom property)
findings.problem: Asked directly whether a second product could be built from this without copying it: not yet, and the gap is narrow and nameable. shell.css does the hard half properly — the ink ladder, the paper ladder, the gap ladder (--gap-hair through --gap-page), leading keyed to role (--lead-label/date/body/title/head/display) and tracking keyed to role (--track-label/data/body/title/head/display) are all named, and that half travels. But the size those roles pair with is a literal at every call site: b.css declares exactly one custom property (--back) and carries 68 hard-coded 'font-size: NNpx' declarations across thirteen values. The thirteen values in elevate.config.json are an inventory ratified after the fact, not a scale — 11, 12 and 13 are three adjacent steps and 15 and 17 are two more, so 'which size is the next one down' has no answer a second team can look up. And every one of the 197 selectors is .b-*, named for this lab's direction letter and this product's nouns: b-rail, b-away, b-horizon, b-behind, b-tick, b-origin. Notes has no horizon and Tasks has nothing behind it. There is no name for the language and no name for its materials, so Home, Notes and Tasks would inherit by copying Timeline's stylesheet and deleting the wedding — which is how three products drift apart.
findings.fix: Two moves, both mechanical. (1) Collapse thirteen sizes to seven and name them on :root beside the leading they already pair with: '--type-label: 11px; --type-data: 13px; --type-body: 15px; --type-title: 17px; --type-head: 24px; --type-display: 38px; --type-hero: 96px', keeping 12/20/30/48/64/148 only as explicitly declared medium overrides (print, phone, the countdown) rather than as peers in the ramp; replace all 68 literals with the tokens and let the audit assert the ramp is the token set, not a list. (2) Split b.css in two: 'language.css' holding the medium-neutral materials under product-neutral names (.sig-plate, .sig-rule, .sig-field, .sig-act, .sig-measure, .sig-tick, .sig-ledger, .sig-undo) and 'timeline.css' holding only what is genuinely about a date and a day. Then name the thing — one page in DIRECTIONS.md stating the four decisions (ground, measure, mono for data, silence until true) as the language's rules. The test is buildable: stand up one Notes screen from language.css alone and see whether it needs a single Timeline selector.

findings.problem: Drove it: with a row's Edit button focused, ArrowDown, ArrowUp, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, End and PageDown are all no-ops — focus does not move and scrollY does not change. The measure is one tab stop per moment. The fixture's seven moments hide it; a wedding-morning running order is thirty to sixty, and the owner then crosses thirty to sixty tab stops to reach the 'Behind you' disclosure below, with no way to jump to the first moment, the last, or the one nearest today. The paid defect library names this class outright ('Roving tab stops — a dense surface is one tab stop per region with arrows inside') and it has come back. It stings twice here because the measure is a spatial instrument: proportional distance is the entire argument of the direction, and the keyboard is the one input with no spatial move in it.
findings.fix: Make the measure one tab stop. Give div[role=list].b-measure a roving model: the row nearest today carries tabindex=0 and every other row tabindex=-1; ArrowDown/ArrowUp move focus one moment later/earlier and scroll it into view; Home focuses the origin, End focuses the horizon, and a bare 't' returns to the moment nearest today. Advertise it once where it is implemented, in the region's existing accessible name ('What is still ahead, nearest first. Use the arrow keys to move between moments.'). Keep Enter opening the editor and Escape returning focus to the row, both of which already work. Add the four key assertions to interaction-check.mjs.

biggestWin: The screen artifact is now internally honest in a way it was not two rounds ago, and that is what holds the score up. Every fact derives through one accessor — the countdown has one owner and three states, the horizon count is the last item on the measure, the arrived count is a word, and the wedding morning draws its past in the product's own language at its own declared scale rather than inventing a second instrument for it. The token layer earns particular credit: leading and tracking are bound to role rather than to size, the gap ladder is declared and used, the editor sheet uses 72dvh rather than 72vh so a phone keyboard cannot bury it, and contrast is measured against the real composited backdrop. That is the discipline of a studio, not of a demo. What stands between it and 9.5 is one unbuilt medium and one unfinished extraction, and neither is a different decision. The keepsake is the urgent one: it is the only thing this product makes that cannot be reflowed after it exists, and it currently has no print stylesheet at all — about a day of work to give it a page, a fold, running furniture, a typeable code and a vocabulary that paper can keep. The extraction is the larger and the more valuable: seven named type steps and a product-neutral component layer, roughly two days, after which Home, Notes and Tasks inherit a language by name instead of inheriting Timeline by copy.
